system_map.overview: A centralised pipeline (CAS Runner) that uses LLM-backed decision-making to continuously steer architecture governance, with compliance checks, state transitions, and persistent knowledge storage.

agents.name: FlowRunner
agents.role: Orchestrates the end-to-end CAS execution flow, coordinating steps and propagating a shared execution context.

agents.name: GovernanceActionService
agents.role: Applies governance actions based on transition rules and agent decisions, invoking compliance checks.

agents.name: LiteLLMClient
agents.role: Provides LLM inference for decision generation and analysis, abstracting multiple providers.

agents.name: MockLLMClient
agents.role: Deterministic LLM client used for testing and CI pipelines without external dependencies.

orchestration.description: A single FlowRunner drives the pipeline sequentially, with each step having a defined contract for input/output and shared context mutation.

tools_and_integrations.name: LiteLLM
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Unified interface to multiple LLM providers, enabling model switching without code changes.

tools_and_integrations.name: MockLLM
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Canned responses for deterministic testing and validation of agentic flows.

tools_and_integrations.name: GitHub Actions
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Automated validation, build, and governance sync workflows that enforce agent output constraints.

tools_and_integrations.name: Knowledge Store
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Persists governance decisions, patterns, rules, and traces for reuse and evidence-based steering.

state_and_memory.description: Governance inventory, decisions, patterns, rules stored in cas-knowledge hierarchy.
Execution context passed between steps in FlowRunner, holding prompts and intermediate results.
Health status and compliance metrics computed from trace metrics and rule contexts.

patterns.name: Central Pipeline Orchestration

tool_protocols.notes: LLM calls are made through the client, not via MCP or tool-calling protocols.

optimisation_targets.notes: Sequential pipeline with shared context ensures deterministic execution and easy tracing.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Centralised orchestration reduces autonomy but improves control and predictability.

patterns.summary: A single FlowRunner executes a sequence of steps, mutating a shared context passed between each phase, ensuring deterministic and traceable execution.
patterns.intent: To coordinate multi-step agentic workflows in a controlled, sequential manner with shared state.
patterns.context: The CAS FlowRunner is the core orchestrator in `src/cas_runner/runner.py`, driving the entire architecture steering flow.
patterns.solution: Implement a central runner that holds a mutable context object and invokes steps in a defined order, each step reading and updating the context.
patterns.reuse_notes: Use for agentic systems requiring deterministic, stepwise orchestration with shared state. Consider adding parallel branches for performance-sensitive steps.

patterns.name: LLM Provider Adapter

tool_protocols.notes: Adapter pattern for LLM providers, not exposing tool-calling.

optimisation_targets.notes: Abstraction allows switching to cheaper or more reliable providers.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Adapter gives flexibility without sacrificing deterministic orchestration.

patterns.summary: LLM clients are abstracted behind a common interface (LiteLLMClient, MockLLMClient) to decouple core logic from specific providers and enable testing.
patterns.intent: To allow swapping LLM providers and using deterministic mocks in tests without changing business logic.
patterns.context: The system includes both LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient in `src/cas_runner/llm/`, suggesting a consistent interface.
patterns.solution: Define a common client interface and provide multiple implementations (LiteLLM for production, Mock for tests) that are injected into the orchestrator.

costs: possible feature loss when switching providers
failure_modes: interface mismatch when adding new providers
mock not representative of real behaviour

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt when the agentic system relies on external LLM calls and requires testability or provider flexibility.

patterns.name: Typed Data Contracts for Agent I/O

tool_protocols.notes: Contracts are Pydantic models, not protocol-based.

optimisation_targets.notes: Typed models ensure data validity and reduce LLM output errors.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Strict contracts limit autonomy but enforce correctness.

patterns.summary: Pydantic models in `steering/models.py` define structured contracts for agent inputs, outputs, and architectural deltas, ensuring type safety and validation.
patterns.intent: To prevent malformed data from flowing between orchestration steps and to formalise the contracts between agent and system.
patterns.context: Steering models like CapabilityRecord, ArchitecturalDelta, and SteeringRuntimeIndex define the data shapes used across the pipeline.
patterns.solution: Use Pydantic models to define all structured data exchanged in the agentic flow, with validation at boundaries.

evidence.note: Typed models for agent data exchange.

failure_modes: over-strict schemas reject legitimate LLM output

patterns.reuse_notes: Apply to any agentic system where LLM outputs are consumed by deterministic code; use schema validation at trust boundaries.

patterns.name: State Transition Registry for Governance

optimisation_targets.notes: Enforces valid transitions to prevent invalid governance actions.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Registry restricts allowed actions, reducing autonomous but dangerous behaviour.

patterns.summary: A TransitionRegistry within GovernanceActionEngine explicitly defines allowed state transitions, acting as a guardrail for governance operations.
patterns.intent: To ensure governance actions only occur when the system is in a valid state, preventing inconsistent or unsafe transitions.
patterns.context: GovernanceActionEngine uses the registry to validate proposed actions against current governance inventory state.
patterns.solution: Centralise allowed transitions in a registry and check before executing any action.

evidence.note: Defines and enforces valid state transitions.

costs: may be too restrictive for novel cases
failure_modes: missing transition rules block legitimate actions

patterns.reuse_notes: Use in agentic systems where actions must be constrained by state to ensure safety and consistency.

patterns.name: Compliance Enforcement Gate

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures governance outputs adhere to predefined rules.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: External gate restricts autonomous actions to compliant ones.

patterns.summary: A ComplianceEngine evaluates agent outputs against governance rules before they are persisted, acting as a gate for quality and safety.
patterns.intent: To prevent non-compliant or unsafe governance decisions from being applied.
patterns.context: GovernanceActionService invokes ComplianceEngine to check findings before performing actions.
patterns.solution: Implement a dedicated engine that runs rules against generated content and returns structured compliance findings.
patterns.reuse_notes: Use as a mandatory checkpoint in agentic pipelines to ensure outputs conform to organisational policies.

patterns.name: Agentic Knowledge Merger

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures new knowledge is integrated without corrupting existing governance.

patterns.summary: AgenticMerger merges agent-generated governance blocks into existing files, preserving structure and avoiding duplication.
patterns.intent: To safely integrate new steering decisions into the persistent governance knowledge base.
patterns.context: The merger is used during bootstrap and governance updates to combine agent output with existing files.
patterns.solution: Implement a dedicated component that reads existing content, applies merge logic, and writes back, preserving governance blocks.
patterns.reuse_notes: Use when agent-generated content must be persistently integrated into structured files (e.g., YAML, Markdown) with existing content.

patterns.name: Health Evaluation Metric for Agentic Systems

tool_protocols.notes: Aggregates metrics into a health score.

optimisation_targets.notes: Provides runtime visibility into system health.

patterns.summary: A health model computes a health status from governance metrics and trace data, providing a dashboard for monitoring agentic system performance.
patterns.intent: To quantify the health of the CAS system in a single score for monitoring and alerting.
patterns.context: The dashboard module includes HealthStatus and calculate_health functions to evaluate governance health.
patterns.solution: Define a health model that aggregates metrics (e.g., compliance rate, throughput) into a status with reasons.
patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt for agentic systems where operational monitoring is needed; design health metrics to be transparent and configurable.

patterns.name: Bootstrap Workspace Initialisation

tool_protocols.notes: Initialises filesystem and merges governance blocks.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures clean start and consistent state.

patterns.summary: A bootstrap process initialises the workspace by creating necessary directories, merging governance blocks, and setting up the environment for agentic execution.
patterns.intent: To guarantee a consistent starting state for the agentic pipeline, reducing environment-specific failures.
patterns.context: CLI entry point calls bootstrap to prepare the CAS workspace before running flows.
patterns.solution: Implement a bootstrap function that creates standard directories, merges governance templates, and validates configuration.
patterns.reuse_notes: Apply to agentic systems that require a well-defined workspace for outputs and state.

patterns.name: CI Workflow Validation Gate

tool_protocols.notes: Static validation of workflow YAML files.

optimisation_targets.notes: Prevents misconfigured CI from breaking builds.

patterns.summary: A Python script (validate_workflows.py) enforces quality standards on GitHub Actions workflows, preventing hardcoding, unpinned installers, and dead code.
patterns.intent: To ensure CI workflows are reproducible, maintainable, and free from common anti-patterns.
patterns.context: This validation script is used in CAS build validation workflows to enforce CI quality.
patterns.solution: Implement static checks that scan workflow YAML for specific patterns (hardcoding, unpinned versions) and fail the build if violations are found.

costs: may reject valid but unconventional workflows

patterns.reuse_notes: Utilise for any agentic or non-agentic project to enforce CI best practices through automated validation.

patterns.name: Persistent Knowledge Base for Agentic Memory

optimisation_targets.notes: Stores governance knowledge for reuse and audit.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Persistent memory enables learning but is static.

patterns.summary: A structured directory hierarchy (cas-knowledge) stores governance decisions, patterns, rules, and traces, acting as the long-term memory of the agentic system.
patterns.intent: To provide a persistent, versioned store for all agent-generated and human-validated knowledge.
patterns.context: The `cas-knowledge` directory contains global governance, project-specific decisions, runtime traces, and templates.
forces: separation of global vs project knowledge
patterns.solution: Organise knowledge into a hierarchical directory structure with clear conventions for governance, patterns, decisions, and runtime data.
patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt in agentic systems that require long-term learning and governance; design with clear taxonomy and versioning.

patterns.name: Mock LLM for Deterministic Testing
patterns.summary: A mock LLM client provides deterministic canned responses, enabling unit and integration tests without external API calls or latency.
patterns.intent: To allow the CAS pipeline to be tested in CI without relying on live LLM services.
patterns.context: MockLLMClient is present alongside LiteLLMClient, suggesting it can be swapped in for tests.
patterns.solution: Implement a mock client that returns preconfigured responses based on input, and allow dependency injection to select it in test configs.

evidence.note: Mock implementation for deterministic LLM responses.

costs: mock behaviour may differ from real LLM

patterns.reuse_notes: Use as part of a provider adapter pattern to enable deterministic testing in agentic applications.

patterns.name: Runtime Trace Persistence

optimisation_targets.notes: Enables post-hoc analysis and health evaluation.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Traces support oversight without constraining agent behaviour.

patterns.summary: The system persists execution traces and evaluation profiles under cas-knowledge/runtime, enabling post-hoc analysis and health scoring.
patterns.intent: To record execution details for debugging, auditing, and computing health metrics.
patterns.context: Runtime directory contains evaluations, traces, and execution-profile.yaml, suggesting a trace capture mechanism.
patterns.solution: Capture key execution events and metrics to files or a structured store for later analysis.

evidence.note: Directory for traces and evaluation data.

failure_modes: missing trace data due to configuration

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt in agentic systems where observability is critical; standardise trace schemas to support tooling.

anti_patterns.name: Hardcoded CI Steps
symptoms: Check zero hardcoding flags hardcoded values in workflows.
Workflow steps embed versions or paths directly.
suggested_remediation: Externalise configuration to variables or environment files.
Use reusable workflows or composite actions to centralise logic.

anti_patterns.name: Unreachable Dry Run in CI
symptoms: Check for unreachable dry-run steps indicates dead code in workflows.
Workflow contains a dry-run that never executes.
impact: Potential security risk if dry-run is bypassed
suggested_remediation: Remove dead branches or make dry-run configurable via inputs.

anti_patterns.name: Unpinned Installer Versions
symptoms: Check for unpinned installers flags missing version pins.
Workflows use installer commands without version constraints.
impact: Intermittent failures due to dependency changes
suggested_remediation: Always pin installer versions in CI workflows.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Typed models and validation via steering models enforce schema on LLM inputs/outputs.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Reduces risk of malformed LLM output affecting downstream steps.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Compliance engine and health model provide static and dynamic evaluation of governance outputs.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Evaluation is a mix of rule-based and metric-driven.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: State transition registry and compliance gate constrain agent actions to valid transitions.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Safety is enforced by design, not post-hoc.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Provider abstraction (LiteLLM) allows switching to cheaper models; mock client reduces test costs.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Cost control is achieved through configurability.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Persistent traces and health metrics provide runtime visibility.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Observability is centralised in the knowledge store.
